newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: One-day strike disrupts Portuguese rail services.
newsitem.headline: One-day strike disrupts Portuguese rail services.

text.p: A one-day rail strike to protest against the restructuring of loss-making state railway company CP-Caminhos de Ferro Portugueses disrupted goods and passenger services across Portugal on Friday, a union spokesman said.
"About 80 percent of Portuguese railway workers, in all lines of work, are taking part in the strike," Jose Manuel Oliveira of the Federation of Portuguese Workers' Unions told Reuters.
"Most goods trains are not circulating. Many passenger trains have been delayed or cancelled across the country," he added.
The Federation includes about 8,000 of Portugal's 14,000 railway workers. Participants in the strike also include railway workers who do not belong to the Federation, Oliveira said.
CP officials confirmed that the strike was taking place but said they had no immediate information about its impact.
Oliveira said the strike was to protest against CP's restructuring plans, excessive working hours and inadequate career structures.
The Socialist government has announced a restructuring plan under which CP would be split into two and private firms allowed to run some operations.
Under the plan, CP would be replaced by one operating company for passenger and freight services and another for infrastructure.
